status: fixed before any code run: what is reproduced, the checks and their thresholds, the arms, the primary comparison and its rule, seeds and stop rules
data: SYNTHETIC. Parameters are the paper's SPX/VIX values (arXiv 2212.10164v1), labelled as such; nothing is calibrated to BTC, which is declared unsupported in this round
paper: Rosenbaum and Zhang, Multi-asset market making under the quadratic rough Heston, arXiv 2212.10164v1

stage_a.what: the paper's control under its Approximation 3.1 (Z and delta frozen, sigma = S0 sqrt(V0)): the exact HJB on an inventory grid against the closed-form asymptotic quadratic value v_hat = -q'Aq - q'B - C(t), and the greedy quoting rule from v_hat

example_1.delta_source: the paper's Example 1 parameter list (Section 4), where delta^1 = 1 and delta^2 = -0.028 are given

example_3.substitution: the paper's 6-asset basket lists only four assets; Example 2's four options are used instead, multi-asset (kappa > 0) against uni-asset (kappa = 0). This is not a reproduction of the paper's figure 4.10, and the conclusions say so
example_3.runs_only_if: checks 1 and 2 pass on examples 1 and 2
example_3.arms: multi-asset: greedy from v_hat with kappa > 0 and kappa_j = kappa/2 on a joint inventory grid. Uni-asset benchmark, the paper's: kappa = 0, kappa_j = kappa/2, exact HJB per asset, the assets run separately on the same random numbers and their P&L summed
example_3.inventory_bound: ours, the paper states none for these options: |q_j| <= 15 m_j = 30 per asset, 31 levels, the level count of example 1's SPX
example_3.delta: frozen at example 2's values; the paper's update of delta every 100 s under the QRH state is not reproduced, and the conclusions say so
example_3.paths_and_interval: as check_2: 5000 paths, paired percentile bootstrap of (multi - uni) P&L, 2000 replicates, 90 %, seed 1111, at each kappa; mean and standard deviation of each arm reported
example_3.role: secondary: reported only, no decision rests on it

check_1.label: our threshold, not the paper's
excluded: cells within 2 levels of an inventory bound, reported apart
check_1.report: the share of cells excluded by each rule
check_1.inconclusive_if: fewer than 50 % of all cells are tested
check_1.refinement: dt/2 and a grid with the inventory bound doubled (31 against 61 levels) each change v by less than 0.5 % on tested cells; otherwise check 1 is not used

constant_C.order: first the exclusions (which depend on v only), then C is set on the tested cells only so that max v_hat = max v over them, the paper's normalisation for its figures
constant_C.fitted_cell: cells at the maxima stay in the 5 % test; the fit makes the error zero only where both maxima fall on one cell, and that cell is not removed
constant_C.reading: check 1 validates shape, not level: its pass is labelled 'control validated (shape)'

check_1.example_2_grid: r is the exact lattice of multiples of 0.002 on [-10, 10], 10001 levels; refinement doubles R (20001 levels); 'within 2 levels of a bound' is within 2 x max step = 2.132 of +/-R

check_2.rule: at each kappa, the paired (approximate - exact) P&L 90 % interval lies wholly within +/- 5 % of |mean exact P&L| at that kappa
check_2.untestable: a kappa whose exact mean P&L interval includes 0 is reported, not tested
check_2.risk: the standard deviation of terminal P&L, reported beside
check_2.paths: the 5 evaluation seeds x 1000 paths = 5000 paths, common random numbers across arms; the design seeds are not used
check_2.interval: paired percentile bootstrap over paths, 2000 replicates, 90 %, seed 1111; the same method gives the exact mean P&L interval used by 'untestable'
check_2.kappa_j: example 1 only: kappa_j = kappa/2 at every kappa of the grid, the paper's Section 4.2.1 choice, which gives 0.005 at kappa 0.01; example 2 has no kappa_j

stage_a.inconclusive_effect: if check 1 or check 2 is inconclusive or fails, the primary comparison still runs and is labelled 'control not validated'; no adopt decision rests on it; if check 1 fails on example 1, stage A stops and is reported

units.rule: sigma^2 per second = S0^2 V0 / (365 x 86400), sigma = 0.2267; the paper gives V0 per year and intensities per second with no conversion
units.sensitivity: a 252 x 6.5 h year, sigma = 0.524, reported beside and outside the rule

alpha.source: the paper's Example 1; for Example 2 the paper does not state it and the same formula is ours

backtest.dynamics: Approximation 3.1 as frozen: one Brownian, dPi = sum over fills of m D/2 + r sigma dW, control held between steps of 0.1 s; T_b = T/2 with the control at horizon T. The paper's QRH-driven backtest is not reproduced in stage A
backtest.arithmetic: fill revenue in exact Decimal; the sigma dW term is a float
backtest.common_random_numbers: for each path seed, one numpy default_rng(SeedSequence([seed, path])) draws before the path starts, independent of any control: one standard normal per step for dW and one uniform per asset, side and step; a posted side fills when its uniform < 1 - exp(-Lambda dt); an unposted side discards its uniform. Every arm reads the same arrays

hjb_dt_s.rule: the exact HJB is solved by explicit backward Euler at dt = 0.1 s, the backtest's step; check 1's refinement 'dt/2' is 0.05 s

primary_comparison.arms: greedy QRH quoting against the crate's GreeksRiskManager delta-limit gate as the post or hold rule, both with the joint delta
primary_comparison.where: at the paper's kappa: example 1 kappa 0.01, example 2 kappa 1
primary_comparison.paths: 5 evaluation seeds x 1000 paths = 5000, common random numbers across arms
primary_comparison.interval: paired percentile bootstrap over paths, 2000 replicates, 90 %, seed 1111
primary_comparison.rule: QRH 'better' only if the whole interval of paired (QRH - gate) P&L lies above 0, 'worse' if wholly below 0; an interval containing 0 is 'no difference shown' and is not a pass

gate_limit.example_2: R = 10 in delta units, the paper's net-risk bound
gate_limit.example_1: per-asset limits Q = (15, 300) and a portfolio delta limit equal to the largest |delta . q| over the inventory box |q_j| <= Q_j, reached with opposite-sign inventories: 15 x 1 + 300 x 0.028 = 23.4 in delta units, from delta_source
gate_limit.sensitivity: x0.5 and x2, one at a time, reported beside and outside the rule

primary_comparison.gate_table: a Rust example over the crate's GreeksRiskManager exports the gate's decision for every inventory state of the grid; both arms then run on the same evaluation paths
primary_comparison.secondary: the other cells of control (greedy, gate) x delta (joint, decoupled: VIX instruments at delta 0), reported as secondary

gate_table_rule.decision: the arm posts only on OrderDecision::Allowed; Scaled counts as hold since sizes are fixed, a choice that can only make the gate trade less, so the share of Scaled states is reported per table
gate_table_rule.breaker: each state is booked, then reset_circuit_breaker is called before check_order, so the table is the limit test alone; the circuit breaker is path dependent and is not modelled, and the README says so
gate_table_rule.example_1_reading: at x1 the 23.4 limit equals the box maximum, so the gate never binds beyond Q and the primary comparison in example 1 is QRH against 'always quote within Q', not against a delta gate; the conclusions say so. x0.5 is the only place it binds, outside the rule
gate_table_rule.tests: a risk-reducing order at the limit gets the decision check_order gives after the reset; the table is identical when states are visited in reversed order
gate_table_rule.scaled_direction: counting Scaled as hold can only reduce the gate arm's trading, which favours QRH if the gate would have earned from those orders; the conclusions give this direction beside the share

secondary_cells.example_1: runnable on the same (q1, q2) grid: the greedy arm uses v_hat computed with delta (1, 0), the gate arm a table with delta (1, 0) and limit 15, the largest |delta . q| over the box under that delta, so that gate never binds beyond Q; all four cells are scored with the joint delta in the sigma dW term, on the same paths, each as a paired interval against (greedy, joint). Reported only
secondary_cells.example_2: declared not runnable before the run: the state is the net risk r under the joint delta, and an SPX-only risk is not a function of r, so a decoupled rule cannot be evaluated on this grid without a 4-dimensional inventory state that the design does not have. The report says 'not runnable' for this cell

stage_b.what: delta from QRH with OptionStratLib 0.24.2 (optionstratlib-simulation 0.24.1): vanilla Monte Carlo, the VIX and VIX futures and options from the factor state, compared with the paper's delta
stage_b.gap: a delta along the model's Brownian is not an OptionStratLib function; it becomes an OptionStratLib issue and is not implemented here. Until it exists, stage B is reported pending, and the conclusions say so
stage_b.stability_gate: every QRH price at 3 seeds and N in {200, 400, 800}: seeds within 2 standard errors, N 400 and 800 within 1 %; a failing row is marked unstable and not used

stage_c.gated_on: stage A passing; not blocked by stage B pending, and while B is pending C makes no quoting or hedging claim
stage_c.what: calibration of QRH (calibrate_quadratic_rough_heston) and of the #96 SVI surface on fixed train strikes and maturities, scored on held-out strikes and maturities and on an unseen-surface scenario with shifted generator parameters

generators.qrh: the well-specified case, which favours QRH by construction, stated
generators.heston: OptionStratLib's heston_walk, not QRH: the fair test

report: compute time per fit and per price

protocol.split: no temporal split: the paths are iid simulations; design seeds and evaluation seeds are fixed apart
protocol.selection: no parameter is fitted in stage A and every kappa is reported

decision.rule: adopt the greedy QRH control only if example 2's primary comparison at x1 and sigma 0.2267 is 'better' and both check 1 and check 2 on example 2 pass; 'worse', 'no difference shown', or any 'control not validated' label means do not adopt in this round
decision.example_1: reported as QRH against 'always quote within Q'; at x1 it is not a test against a delta gate and cannot support adoption
decision.scope: the decision covers the control under Approximation 3.1 with the paper's delta on the SPX/VIX parameters only. It is reported with compute cost, fit quality, risk and model limits. No pricing or hedging adoption while stage B is pending; BTC is not evaluable in this round

compute.stages_b_c: 1 to 2 h on 1 or 2 processes, slots asked for
compute.builds: nice'd and serial while the machine is at its cap

changes: before any code run, from review: the wording of example 1's gate limit, now the maximum of |delta . q| over the inventory box; the number is unchanged

before any code run, from review: units, alpha, the order and reading of C in check 1, example 2's exact lattice, backtest dynamics and common random numbers. When the unit was chosen only the hand estimate of A (annual sigma gives A about 45 against D/2 = 0.125) was computed from the paper's formula; no HJB, check or P&L had been run
before any code run, from review: the gate table's decision rule (Allowed only, Scaled share reported), the breaker left out by a reset per state, example 1's reading at x1, and two tests

before any code run on the paper's examples, from review: check 2's paths, seeds and interval; the HJB's base dt; kappa_j = kappa/2 across the kappa grid; an explicit decision rule resting on example 2; Scaled's direction; example 3's arms and its inventory bound; the decoupled cells, with example 2's declared not runnable
